alignments.note: Construct noun of the superscription; the indefinite article belongs to the nominal expression under rule 15.
Article on the rectum; the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase, so the morpheme is unrepresented under rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's *of* under rule 19, headed on the noun.

One substantive rendered by a multi-word phrase: *time* is the generic the ASV supplies to complete the quantifier, so the head stays on *Many* under rule 31. The margin's *Or, Much* was read and set aside under rule 38.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.
Object suffix realized by *me* under rule 18.

The ASV writes the ablative as the discontinuous circumposition *from ... up*; both words belong to the one preposition under rules 24 and 25, headed on *from*, which carries the relation. The competing reading marks *up* `added` under rule 30; I took the preposition's, since English writes *from my youth up* as one relational frame and no other morpheme answers to the word.
Jussive rendered by the volitive frame *Let ... say*; the framing word joins the verb's unit under rule 17, discontinuous around the subject and particle under rule 25, headed on the lexical verb.
Proper name as subject of the jussive.

review_notes: The superscription is aligned as ordinary source text: `שִׁיר` takes the supplied *A* under rule 15 and the article on `מַעֲלוֹת` is unrepresented for want of a written *the*.
`מִן` is read as the discontinuous *from ... up*; the alternative leaving *up* `added` is named in that unit's note.
